item.research_question: How does deep multi-element co-substitution of Fe3+ cations with Al3+, Co3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, and In3+ affect the phase stability, crystal structure, and magnetic properties of SrFe12O19 hexaferrites?
item.material_system: SrFe12O19 hexaferrite deeply substituted up to at.67% by Al3+, Co3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, and In3+ cations (samples A1–A6 identified as single-phase)
item.processing_route: Conventional solid-phase synthesis: mixing Fe2O3, Ga2O3, Al2O3, Cr2O3, In2O3, CoO, and SrCO3; hand grinding in agate mortar for 30 min; planetary milling for 6 h; pressing at 5 tons force (8×5 mm cylinders); sintering at 1400°C for 5 h on platinum substrate under alundum crucible
item.test_conditions: XRD (5°–90°, Cu-Kα, room temperature); SQUID magnetometry (field up to 16 kOe at 300 K; temperature up to 400 K in 1.6 kOe; ZFC/FC in 300 Oe)
key_findings: Six single-phase samples (A1–A6) were obtained, while others formed non-single-phase products.
Unit cell volume varied from V ≈ 648.21(17) Å³ (sample A6) to V ≈ 694.13(18) Å³ (sample A4).
Average grain size ranged from 2 to 5 μm, with porosity not exceeding ~4%.
Saturation magnetization (Ms) at 300 K ranged from ~1 emu/g (A6) to ~5 emu/g (A4), with a maximum of Ms ≈ 43 emu/g recorded for A5 at 100 K.
Magnetic ordering temperature (Tmo) varied from ~80 K (A6 in 1.6 kOe) to ~381.8 K (A3 in 1.6 kOe).
Freezing temperature (Tf) ranged from ~77 K (A5) to ~341 K (A3).
Average magnetic cluster size was estimated at ~350–400 nm.
All magnetization curves were nonmonotonic with respect to the average ionic radius ⟨rM⟩.
item.mechanism: Deep co-substitution leads to magnetic dilution and inhomogeneous distribution of cations, which weakens the Fe3+(M3+)–O2−–Fe3+(M3+) indirect superexchange interactions despite some reduction in bond lengths, resulting in a frustrated magnetic state composed of magnetically disordered nanosized clusters within a magnetically ordered matrix.
item.limitations: The study relied solely on XRD for structural analysis, which provides only average behavior; detailed local structure and cation distribution require Mössbauer spectroscopy and neutron diffraction. Additionally, only the cheapest solid-phase method was used without optimizing annealing, cooling rates, or pressure.
item.future_work: The authors plan to perform Mössbauer spectroscopy and powder neutron diffraction to determine the exact distribution of substituting cations over nonequivalent crystallographic positions and to refine the understanding of exchange interactions.
quotes: Deep co-substitution of the Fe3+ iron cations in SrFe12O19 strontium hexaferrite with M3+ triply charged diamagnetic Al3+, Ga3+, and In3+, as well as paramagnetic Co3+, and Cr3+ cations leads to a weakening of the Fe3+(M3+) – O2− – Fe3+(M3+) indirect superexchange and forms the frustrated magnetic state
The average size of magnetic clusters varied around ∼350 nm.
All the plotted dependencies are nonmonotonic.
